newsitem.title: CHINA: China says European talks on jet move smoothly.
newsitem.headline: China says European talks on jet move smoothly.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng said on Monday that talks with France and its European partners on production of a 100-seat passenger jet were progressing well.
He also said that successful cooperation on the project would be an important step forward in Sino-French and Sino-European cooperation.
Li made the remarks during a meeting with French Minister of Equipment, Housing, Transport and Tourism Bernard Pons, the official Xinhua news agency said.
China signed a letter of intent with France's Societe Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale in April to study building a 100-seat passenger jet for China's domestic market.
The accord was reached during a visit to France by the Chinese premier.
Aerospatiale's partners in the project are British Aerospace Plc and Alenia, a unit of Finmeccanica.
The French minister was quoted as saying there was a consensus between France and its European partners that cooperation with China in aircraft manufacturing should be vigorously promoted.
The French government was willing to work along with companies to put the project into operation, Xinhua quoted Pons as saying.
Li also told Pons that China and France should promote all-round ties and continue international cooperation.
He singled out nuclear power cooperation as another area of major progress. France's Framatome SA has been the main supplier on the Daya Bay nuclear power plant in southern China.
The Chinese premier also said he welcomed a planned visit to Beijing next year by French President Jacques Chirac.
"We are looking forward to President Chirac's China visit next May, with a belief that his visit will enhance the friendly bilateral ties between the two countries," Li said.
